questions.question:
In the Rabin-Karp algorithm, the hashing technique is used to:
a) store the string
b) calculate the matching of substrings
c) compare every substring
d) search for substrings by calculating hash values

options.D: search for substrings by calculating hash values

questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp uses hash values of substrings for fast comparison — only when hash values match does it verify character-by-character.

questions.question:
The Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) string matching algorithm preprocesses the pattern to:
a) avoid rechecking the matched characters
b) compare characters from the end
c) skip unmatched characters entirely
d) directly match the substring
questions.explanation: KMP preprocesses the pattern to build the LPS (Longest Proper Prefix which is also Suffix) array, avoiding re-comparisons of already matched characters.

questions.question:
What is a Rabin and Karp Algorithm?
a) String Matching Algorithm
b) Shortest Path Algorithm
c) Spanning Tree Algorithm
d) Approximation Algorithm
questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp is a string matching algorithm that uses rolling hash functions to find pattern occurrences in text efficiently.

questions.question:
What is a Rabin and Karp Algorithm?
a) String Matching Algorithm
b) Shortest Path Algorithm
c) Minimum spanning tree Algorithm
d) Approximation Algorithm
questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp is a string matching algorithm that uses hashing to find any one of a set of pattern strings in a text.

What is the worst-case time complexity of the Naive (Brute Force) String Matching algorithm?
a) O(n)
b) O(m)
c) O(n × m)
d) O(n + m)
questions.explanation: Naive String Matching compares the pattern (length m) at every position in the text (length n), giving O(n × m) worst case.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of the KMP string matching algorithm?
a) O(n × m)
b) O(n + m)
c) O(n²)
d) O(m²)
questions.explanation: KMP runs in O(n + m) — O(m) for building the LPS array and O(n) for scanning the text, never re-comparing matched characters.

questions.question:
What is the worst-case time complexity of the Rabin-Karp algorithm?
a) O(n + m)
b) O(n × m)
c) O(n log m)
d) O(m²)
questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp worst case is O(n × m) — occurs when all hash values match (spurious hits), requiring character-by-character verification each time.

questions.question:
Horspool's string matching algorithm compares the pattern with text in which direction?
a) Left to right
b) Right to left
c) From the middle outward
d) Random order
questions.explanation: Horspool's algorithm compares characters from right to left (starting from the last character of the pattern), using a bad character shift table.

questions.question:
The Boyer-Moore string matching algorithm uses which of the following heuristics?
a) Bad character heuristic only
b) Good suffix heuristic only
c) Both bad character and good suffix heuristics
d) Rolling hash function

options.C: Both bad character and good suffix heuristics

questions.explanation: Boyer-Moore uses both Bad Character and Good Suffix heuristics together, choosing the larger shift to skip maximum characters.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity to search for a word of length L in a Trie?
a) O(n)
b) O(L)
c) O(n × L)
d) O(log n)
questions.explanation: Trie search follows one node per character — a word of length L requires exactly L node traversals, giving O(L) time complexity.

questions.question:
Which sorting algorithm is most commonly used for sorting strings?
a) Quick Sort
b) Merge Sort
c) MSD Radix Sort
d) Bubble Sort
questions.explanation: MSD (Most Significant Digit) Radix Sort is commonly used for string sorting — it sorts character by character from the first position.

questions.question:
In regular expressions, the symbol '*' (Kleene star) means:
a) Exactly one occurrence of the preceding element
b) Zero or more occurrences of the preceding element
c) One or more occurrences of the preceding element
d) Optional occurrence of the preceding element

options.A: Exactly one occurrence of the preceding element
options.B: Zero or more occurrences of the preceding element
options.C: One or more occurrences of the preceding element
options.D: Optional occurrence of the preceding element

questions.explanation: Kleene star (*) matches zero or more occurrences of the preceding element — it is the most fundamental repetition operator in regex.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a lossless data compression technique?
a) JPEG compression
b) MP3 compression
c) Huffman Coding
d) Video streaming compression
questions.explanation: Huffman Coding is a lossless compression technique — it uses variable-length codes based on character frequency, preserving all original data.

b) Rolling hash

questions.explanation: Rabin-Karp uses a rolling hash to update the hash value in O(1) by removing the old leading character and adding the new trailing character.

questions.question:
In the KMP algorithm, if the pattern is P = "AABAAC", what is the LPS (failure function) array?
a) [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
b) [0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 0]
c) [0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2]
d) [0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3]
questions.explanation: For P = "AABAAC": A→0, AA→1, AAB→0, AABA→1, AABAA→2, AABAAC→0. The LPS array is [0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 0].

What is the best-case time complexity of the Boyer-Moore string matching algorithm?
a) O(n × m)
b) O(n + m)
c) O(n / m)
d) O(n)
questions.explanation: Boyer-Moore's best case is O(n/m) — by using the bad character and good suffix heuristics, it can skip large portions of the text.

questions.question:
Horspool's algorithm is a simplified version of which algorithm?
a) KMP Algorithm
b) Rabin-Karp Algorithm
c) Boyer-Moore Algorithm
d) Naive String Matching
questions.explanation: Horspool's algorithm is a simplified Boyer-Moore — it uses only the bad character heuristic (on the rightmost text character in the window) for shifting.

a) Completely random characters
b) Many unique characters
c) Long runs of repeated characters

questions.explanation: RLE replaces consecutive repeated characters with a count and the character — it is most effective when data contains long runs of the same character.
